title: Perf Gate Rollout Plan (Q1 2026) — Release Train Phases & Rollback
content:
Slide 1 — Title
Perf Gate Rollout Plan (Q1 2026)
Phased introduction for runtime performance regression gates across CI + release candidates
Owners: Release Engineering (Connor O’Brien), CI/Nightly Automation (Sahana Iyer)

Slide 2 — Why we’re doing this (problem statement)
- Runtime perf regressions have been caught late (post-merge, sometimes post-release) due to:
  - inconsistent benchmark coverage
  - unclear regression vs noise definitions
  - lack of reproducible baselines tied to release candidates
- Goal: make performance a first-class release requirement without destabilizing the release train.
- This rollout plan focuses on change-management: phased enforcement + clean rollback.

Slide 3 — Scope (what the gate covers)
In scope metrics (baseline suite):
- Latency: TTFT (p50/p95/p99), E2E latency (p95/p99 where applicable)
- Decode rate proxy: TPOT (p50/p95/p99)
- Throughput: tokens/sec at steady state; completed req/sec for fixed-shape workloads
- Reliability guardrails: error rate, timeouts, load-shedding counters (as “safety” signals)

In scope surfaces:
- Runtime PRs (selected paths)
- Release candidates (RC) for runtime release train
- Nightly perf-canary (baseline suite execution)

Out of scope (for Q1):
- Full model catalog publication gating
- Customer-facing dashboards/attestation
- Non-runtime repos (SDKs, Console) unless they change perf-critical server behavior

Slide 4 — Non-goals (explicit)
- Not attempting to gate every PR on the full workload suite in Q1.
- Not attempting to “solve” all fleet variance; we will enforce environment pinning + variance budgets.
- Not attempting to optimize for minimum wall-clock on day one; correctness and trust first.

Slide 5 — Definitions / language used in this deck
- Baseline: locked Q1 2026 reference results for a given (model x hardware x region x traffic shape)
- Gate check: automated comparison of current results to baseline + variance budget rules
- Warn-only: signal only; does not affect merge/release
- Soft fail: check fails; merge/release allowed with explicit override + sign-off
- Hard fail: check fails; blocks merge/release except via emergency break-glass

Slide 6 — Inputs this plan depends on
- Perf baseline suite + taxonomy is the “source of truth” for what we measure
  - See: perf-baseline-q1-2026-overview + traffic-shapes taxonomy
- Variance budgets define allowable drift/noise bands per metric
  - See: benchmark-methodology-and-variance-budget
- Company regression policy defines thresholds + exception process
  - See: perf-regression-policy-q1-2026

Slide 7 — Where gates run (systems view)
1) Nightly perf-canary:
- Runs representative suite on pinned environments
- Stores artifacts + posts diffs (Slack + dashboard)
- Primary signal for baseline drift

2) CI “perf smoke” job on runtime PRs:
- Small subset (fast, high-signal) to catch obvious regressions early
- Produces structured artifacts perf-canary can ingest

3) Release candidate (RC) qualification:
- Full baseline suite run is required for RCs once we reach Phase 2+

Slide 8 — Rollout principles
- Start with trust-building: visibility + triage muscle before enforcement.
- Ramp enforcement by:
  1) metric severity (p95 before p99; latency before throughput)
  2) workload criticality (top-served + incident-linked shapes first)
  3) confidence in variance (only enforce where variance budget is stable)
- Keep a clean rollback path at each phase.

Slide 9 — Phase overview (timeline)
Phase 0 (Weeks 1–3): Plumbing + visibility
Phase 1 (Weeks 4–6): Warn-only gates
Phase 2 (Weeks 7–9): Soft fail gates (override + sign-off)
Phase 3 (Weeks 10–12): Hard fail gates (blocking)

Note: exact week boundaries can slide by 1 week depending on baseline lock date.

Slide 10 — Phase 0: Plumbing + visibility (Weeks 1–3)
Entry criteria:
- Benchmark runner produces stable output schema (commit SHA, build metadata, env pins)
- Dashboards show model/region/hardware/shape breakdown
- Variance study establishes budgets for top shapes (at minimum)

Work items:
- Integrate artifact stamping for reproducibility (runtime build + CUDA/driver)
- Confirm metric pipeline correctness for TTFT/TPOT (streaming edge cases included)
- Configure Slack notifications for nightly diffs (summary + links)

Exit criteria:
- Nightly jobs run reliably with <10% flake rate (job success, not perf)
- On-call/SRE agrees on alert routing and ownership

Owners:
- Release Eng: Connor O’Brien
- CI/Nightly: Sahana Iyer
- Runtime perf suite: Marcus Reed, Kira Volkov
- SRE (variance + paging): Sean Gallagher
- Telemetry validation: Logan Wright / Nadia Rahman (consulted)

Slide 11 — Phase 1: Warn-only gates (Weeks 4–6)
What changes:
- PR perf smoke becomes a required CI job but is non-blocking (warn-only status)
- Nightly baseline drift alerts are “informational” (no paging; routed to #eng-runtime + #eng-releases)

Coverage (initial):
- 2–3 top models
- 3–4 traffic shapes (incl. streaming chat, bursty concurrency, long-context)
- Single primary region per hardware to reduce noise

Decision policy:
- Any “severe” regression triggers a triage ticket, but does not block merges.

Exit criteria:
- We complete at least 10 business days of warn-only data
- Top recurring false-positive causes are addressed (fleet drift, metric bugs, config mismatch)

Slide 12 — Phase 2: Soft fail gates (Weeks 7–9)
What changes:
- Nightly perf drift is now a release-train signal:
  - If drift exceeds regression thresholds, release candidate requires explicit approval to proceed
- PR perf smoke becomes soft-fail on protected branches:
  - Failing PR can merge only with override + sign-off

Override requirements (soft fail):
- Must link:
  - perf diff artifact
  - root-cause hypothesis OR justification (expected change)
  - mitigation plan (follow-up ticket)
- Sign-off required from:
  - Runtime perf architect (Noah Patel) OR Runtime exec sponsor delegate (Mateo Alvarez)
  - Release Engineering (Connor O’Brien) for RCs
  - SRE lead (Sean Gallagher) if tail latency metrics are implicated

Exit criteria:
- Overrides are rare and well-documented (target: <15% of failing signals)
- Triage loop time <48 hours for high-severity regressions

Slide 13 — Phase 3: Hard fail gates (Weeks 10–12)
What changes:
- PR perf smoke is blocking for runtime perf-critical changes
- RC qualification requires a passing baseline suite run across agreed matrix

Break-glass policy (hard fail):
- Used only for:
  - Sev0/Sev1 production mitigation
  - security fixes that cannot wait
- Requires:
  - Release Eng approval (Connor O’Brien) + Runtime exec sponsor (Mateo Alvarez)
  - follow-up retro + baseline re-run within 24 hours

Slide 14 — What gets gated first (ordered list)
Gating order (initial enforcement set):
1) TTFT p95 (streaming + non-streaming)
2) TPOT p95
3) Error rate / timeout rate guardrail (must not exceed budget)
4) TTFT p99 for shapes with stable variance
5) Throughput (tokens/sec) once we stabilize fleet normalization

Slide 15 — Regression thresholds (initial proposal)
We will use the company perf regression policy as the canonical rule-set.
Initial enforcement bands (subject to variance budget doc):
- Latency regressions:
  - p95: > +5% vs baseline AND outside variance budget
  - p99: > +8% vs baseline AND outside variance budget (phase in later)
- TPOT regressions:
  - p95: > +5% vs baseline (slower) AND outside variance budget
- Throughput regressions:
  - > -5% vs baseline AND outside variance budget
- Reliability guardrail:
  - error rate or timeouts: any statistically significant increase above baseline (shape-specific)

Notes:
- “Outside variance budget” is required to prevent gating on noise.
- Where variance budgets are not yet stable, metrics remain warn-only.

Slide 16 — Workload suite subset for CI (perf smoke)
Requirements for CI subset:
- Total runtime < 20 minutes per PR (target 10–15)
- High signal-to-noise
- Covers both scheduler/batching and kernel hot paths

Proposed CI shapes:
- Streaming chat, mixed prompt lengths, moderate concurrency ramp
- Non-streaming short-form, high QPS (batching pressure)
- Long-context streaming (tail risk) at low concurrency

Slide 17 — Repo/path-based gating (what triggers perf smoke)
Perf smoke runs automatically when PR touches:
- scheduler / batching codepaths
- kernel selection / autotune settings
- KV cache behavior, eviction/compaction
- telemetry timestamps for TTFT/TPOT

Perf smoke does NOT run by default for:
- comments/docs
- Console-only changes
- non-runtime components (unless explicitly requested)

Manual trigger label:
- “run-perf-smoke” label can force run

Slide 18 — Ownership / RACI (who does what)
Accountable:
- Connor O’Brien (Release Engineering): policy enforcement on release train; break-glass approvals
- Sahana Iyer (CI/Nightly): CI + nightly job reliability; retry/failure classification

Responsible:
- Marcus Reed / Kira Volkov: baseline suite + harness maintenance; triage support
- Runtime teams (Hiro Tanaka, Sofia Ivanova, Omar El-Sayed): root-cause + fixes

Consulted:
- Sean Gallagher: variance/paging, fleet drift processes
- Jonas Weber / Sana Farid: methodology, stats, confidence intervals
- Allison Grant / Sergio Costa: dashboards + alert rules

Informed:
- Runtime org + oncall rotations; Product (Henry Cho / Paula Mendes) for any externally shared metrics

Slide 19 — Triage flow (when a gate fires)
1) Gate fires → artifact link generated automatically (diff view + raw JSON)
2) Assign triage owner based on likely component:
   - Kernel deltas: Hiro Tanaka / Grace Kim
   - Scheduling/batching deltas: Sofia Ivanova / Lena Fischer / Julian Moore
   - KV cache/tail: Omar El-Sayed / Samir Qureshi
   - Telemetry: Logan Wright / Nadia Rahman
   - Fleet drift: Vanessa Ortiz / SRE
3) Confirm whether this is:
   - real regression
   - expected perf shift (intentional)
   - measurement issue (flake, env drift, metric bug)
4) Decide action:
   - revert
   - fix-forward
   - override (Phase 2+ only) + documented follow-up

Slide 20 — Rollback plan (critical)
Rollback trigger conditions:
- High false positive rate: >25% of gate failures determined to be noise/measurement over 5 business days
- CI instability: perf smoke causes >5% incremental CI failure rate (infrastructure, not perf)
- Release-train blockage not proportional to value (qualitative call by Release Eng + Runtime sponsor)

Rollback actions (ordered, minimal to maximal):
1) Reduce enforcement scope (drop p99, drop throughput; keep warn-only)
2) Narrow matrix (single region/hardware) until variance source is resolved
3) Switch hard fail → soft fail (temporary)
4) Switch soft fail → warn-only (temporary)

Rollback execution owners:
- Connor O’Brien (decision + comms)
- Sahana Iyer (CI config changes)
- Sean Gallagher (paging/alert adjustments)

Rollback comms:
- Post in #eng-releases + #eng-runtime with:
  - what changed
  - why
  - when we’ll re-enable enforcement

Slide 21 — Communication plan
- Weekly release-train update (5 min): current phase, top regressions, override count
- Dedicated Slack thread per significant regression with artifact links
- Monthly retro: what gates caught, what we missed, what was noisy

Audiences:
- Runtime engineers (primary)
- Release train participants (release captains, oncall)
- SRE/Observability (variance + dashboards)
- Product (for messaging / transparency requests)

Slide 22 — Risks & mitigations
Risk: GPU fleet variance / driver drift causes false regressions
Mitigation:
- strict env pinning for baseline jobs; drift detection; quarantine hosts

Risk: kernel autotune nondeterminism
Mitigation:
- pin seeds + reduce autotune jitter; prefer deterministic kernel paths for baseline-critical workloads

Risk: metric bugs (TTFT for streaming)
Mitigation:
- telemetry validation harness + periodic audits vs client-measured timings

Risk: too much metric cardinality cost
Mitigation:
- pre-aggregated dimensions for dashboards; limit per-tenant breakout

Slide 23 — Decision points / asks
- Confirm enforcement start date for Phase 1 (warn-only) on PR perf smoke
- Approve initial CI subset workloads (3 shapes) and time budget
- Confirm sign-off roster for soft-fail overrides (names + delegates)
- Confirm which regions/hardware are “release-train standard” for Q1 baseline

Slide 24 — Open questions (tracked)
- Do we enforce separate thresholds for streaming vs non-streaming TTFT?
- How do we treat improvements that increase variance (e.g., aggressive batching heuristics)?
- How do we formalize “expected perf shift” for a feature that trades latency for throughput?
- When to expand matrix (multi-region) without causing noise-driven gating?

Slide 25 — Appendix: Proposed phase gates checklist
Phase 0 readiness checklist:
- [ ] baseline artifact stamping includes: runtime SHA, benchmark-lab SHA, CUDA/driver, instance type
- [ ] dashboards show p50/p95/p99 TTFT/TPOT with shape/model breakdown
- [ ] variance budgets exist for initial enforced metrics

Phase 1 readiness checklist:
- [ ] CI job exists, stable, and produces artifacts
- [ ] Slack summary posts include a single canonical artifact link

Phase 2 readiness checklist:
- [ ] override mechanism implemented (label + sign-off)
- [ ] release qualification checklist updated to reference baseline suite

Phase 3 readiness checklist:
- [ ] break-glass documented and tested
- [ ] rollback switch verified (hard fail -> soft fail) within 30 minutes
